we identified the gene toolkit involved in sex determination and maintenance in sparids.

the comparative analysis of sex-biased genes and pathways in gonads and brains of gonochoristic and hermaphroditic sparid fishes reveals common male and female specific gene sets that are probably implicated to sex-maintenance in these fish.
we found a gene toolkit that is implicated in functional sex in Sparidae hermaphrodites, by comparative transcriptomics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes involved in sex maintenance and sex change in Sparidae, a family of fish with a remarkable diversity in the way the sexes are established.

the identification of sex-biased transcripts in two species of sparid fish, the gonochorist Dentex dentex and the protandric hermaphrodites Sparus aurata, through the construction and analysis of gonadal and brain transcriptomes.

the study of the molecular basis of sex determination and differentiation in the family of Sparidae, which includes the gilthead seabram (Sparus auratus), one of the most relevant species in Mediterranean aquaculture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the genes that are differentially expressed between sexes in Sparidae are those that are implicated in sex maintenance and that the sex-specific expression of these genes seems to be a common trait in all species studied.

the gene expression profiles of the brain and gonads of the common dentex (male gonochoristic species) and gilthead seabram (protandrous hermophrodite species) were differentially affected by the sex phenotype and the sex-determining mechanism, and that the genes that were differentially regulated were involved in the sex maintenance of the species.

sex-biased genes in Sparidae are not only implicated in gonad development and function, but are also involved in other physiological processes, such as the control of metabolism, the immune response, or the response to stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the genes and pathways that were found to be sex-biased in gonads and brains of gonochoristic and hermaphrodites species of Sparidae are likely to be involved in the maintenance of the functional sex.
the sex determination pathway seems to have been conserved in Sparidae, but the sex maintenance pathways seem to have evolved in parallel in gonochoristic and hermaphrodites.
the sex-biases in the gonad and brain transcriptomes of two sparids (one gonochoristic and one hermaphroditic species) have been characterized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sex-biased genes are conserved across different reproductive modes in sparids, suggesting a common genetic basis of sex determination in the family.
the genes implicated in sex maintenance in sparid species are conserved and that the sex phenotype is established through the modulation of gene expression.

the genes involved in the maintenance of the functional sex are conserved across the different Sparidae species, which opens the door to the development of a common gene toolkit for controlling the sex phenotype in aquaculture.
